apps.next: 20 NOV, AHEAD OF IT'S KEYS (#492, v72) AND THE CHECKS THAT OUTLIVE A CHAT (#495). The merge that made Ahead of It out of three apps left the house block pointing at its predecessor's key, so a date sent from ANY app's tell box never arrived — driven, not read: on a phone with only aheadofit_v1 it said “Ahead of It isn’t set up on this phone yet” and offered One Thing instead; on a phone with ahead_v1 it wrote where the merged app reads only on first run. aheadKey() now writes where the list actually is. The backup registry also lost the legacy keys and the papers pocket, so Start fresh left three old lists behind and the next open migrated them back in; it now names all four keys and idb:['ahead_papers']. The prefixes are deliberately NOT listed — steward_ could be another app's. The Ahead of It chat verified v72 with its own harness: all four keys erased, pocket gone, reopen lands on a true first open. MY OWN HARNESS COULD NOT DRIVE START FRESH and I said so rather than claim it; that chat found why — the house claims window.djStartFresh at 0, 300 and 1500 ms because an older erase layer at the end of the page assigns after it, so calling early drives the old layer's guessed key names. SO THE CHECKS NOW LIVE IN THE REPO: tools/house/test.cjs, 21 of them, own static server, `node tools/house/test.cjs` — back, mic, tell, same. Its README carries the two traps that made earlier runs lie (a service worker's own fetch is not intercepted by Playwright routes, so a reload grades the deployed site; file:// is not what a phone loads). Start fresh is the one thing in reach not covered; the Ahead of It chat is invited to land its harness alongside. 20 NOV, THE PHONE’S BACK (#481, house v70): five chats — The Church App, Pit Wall, Compass, On Guard and the sweep chat — each measured the same gap in v68 within an hour and all read the code right. v68 gave an app the chip and nothing else: popstate returned early unless a house sheet was open, and the only pushState lived inside sheet(), so there was no history entry for the phone’s Back to consume. Now one history entry covers the whole trail whoever started it (djHistOn on the first push or the first house sheet, djHistOff when the last thing closes) and popstate walks DJ_BACK whenever there is anything on it — no app change needed. Three more: DJ_MARK records the depth when the first house sheet opens so closing one no longer takes the app’s entries (On Guard’s case: ? Help over Mail, tap outside, lose Home); djBack.navigating() is exposed and push ignores a push while it is set; and the house’s chip counts only entries above the mark so it can never pop an app screen. Every dismissal goes through djHouseClose() — the ? toggle, both sheets’ Close, both backdrops, the rows that leave the house. DELIBERATE, NOT A BUG: the AI confirm sheet to its answer is one screen, not two, because Back from a finished answer would offer to send it again — My Circle asked; it is settled. 17 checks in Chromium, all passing; djBack code byte-identical in all 54. The sweep chat and Pit Wall were told; app chats that wrote “phone Back cannot work” on a card should take it off, and On Guard should remove its own capture-phase popstate or it will step back twice on one press. 20 NOV, THE MICROPHONE (#462, merged): Jerry on his Mac in Chrome — “I hit the microphone, and the microphone would shut off after every word.” Chrome ends a recognition session at the first pause unless continuous is on. In the house block’s talk() it was on only for a <textarea>, so every one-line box stopped after a word, and the Tell it sheet never set it at all. Both now: continuous on for every box, a session Chrome closes started again with the words already typed as the new base (a fresh session restarts e.results from empty), and four seconds of silence to finish — nothing else would end it now. no-speech and aborted no longer tear it down; not-allowed still does and says so. House block is v69. Tested against a stub recogniser, not a real microphone: whether it sounds right is Jerry on a real device. 20 NOV, THE BACK BUTTON (#454, merged): Jerry, relayed from the Family Money chat — “If you go one screen too far or something, you can’t go back to the previous one”, and “Look at all the apps and make sure we have the same button there when we need to have it.” There is no shared screen system to hang that on: all 54 apps roll their own (show, go, open*, sheet, modal, panel, and 14 with none of them). So the house block, now v68, carries the mechanism and uses it for its own screens — window.djBack.push(fn), .button(), .go(), .depth(). Anything opened through the house sheet() gets the chip and the wiring free, the chip shows only when there is somewhere to go, and the phone’s own Back and the edge swipe step back through house screens instead of leaving the app. Wired: the ? menu through to Which AI, Recent problems and Help. THE BIGGER HALF IS NOT DONE — each app’s own screens must call djBack.push where one screen leads to another, and most of those apps belong to other chats, so it went to the front door (Store Manager) to route, relayed 20 Nov. Cheapest first, each has a single funnel: jarbyjar, tripstab, ourtable (box), nownext (box), thekey (sheet). familydash already has its own (v9.0, #452). Do not wire another chat’s app from here; widen the API if one asks. THIS CARD WAS OVERWRITTEN ONCE, on 20 Nov, with the Family Money Dashboard’s text (commit e9480d57) — restored here from e54948cf. If it happens again, the Family Money card is row 63, this one is row 54. Nothing waiting on Jerry. 18 NOV, THE CAP: the door stopped the Family Money Dashboard halfway through a statement folder with 7 PDFs left, so Jerry raised it from 40 asks a day per household to 200 (#423) and redeployed the Worker himself — the door is serving 200 now. IT IS NOT USABLE YET, and that is not on him: familydash/index.html hardcodes 40 in four places and counts to 40 with its own doorLeft(), so the Dashboard still stops at 40 until its chat follows. Daraja · Family Money Dashboard (session_01SneDTbsK4SkYWEXXimsAkK) was told by relay on 18 Nov, with the four line numbers. Do not fix it here. PARKED UNTIL JUST BEFORE THE STORE GOES LIVE, Jerry’s call on 18 Nov: “Put it on the to do list and record it just before we go live with the store.” THE JOB — change the round dock button from “?” to the letters AI with a sparkle badge, and bring the 33 video lines that name it along in the same piece of work. Five layouts were rendered at the real 44px and he chose the sparkle as a BADGE ABOVE THE LETTERS — not sitting on them, which took the top off the A, and not stacked inside the circle, which shrank the letters to fit. THE CODE CHANGE, written and tested once then reverted: in dock()’s toggleBtn, replace textContent = ‘?’ with innerHTML of AI plus an absolutely-positioned span at top:-4px right:-4px, font-size 16px, line-height 1, pointer-events none, holding the sparkle and marked aria-hidden; set aria-label to “Ask an AI, help and settings”; and add position:relative and overflow:visible to the front of its cssText. Checked across 8 apps at 390px: the badge renders 20x16, sits 7px clear of the right edge, nothing clips it (#djDock sets no overflow and holds a 10px margin from the edge), the menu still opens, no page errors. The sheet’s own heading stays Help and settings, which is still true. WHY IT DID NOT SHIP ON THE DAY: 33 spoken lines across about 25 apps say “the question mark button in the corner has the tour and help” — advent, everyday, ourtable x2, jarbyjar x2, whoscoming x2, nownext, ahead, nextstep, breakeven, safety, storykeeper, academy, thekey, compass, drumbeat, pitwall, ff, churchserve x2, churchdrive x2, churchclubhouse x2, churchgameday x2, churchkey x2, npreceipts, rafiki x2, all in firsttime or train. THE DARAJA AI DOOR IS LIVE AND ANSWERING — tested end to end by Jerry on 17 Nov: he tapped the ? in an app, chose “Ask an AI about this screen”, saw “Sending to Daraja’s own AI”, tapped Send it, and an answer came back. So all 54 apps now ask Claude directly instead of asking the person to copy and paste. HOW IT IS SET UP, confirmed on the Cloudflare Settings page: the Worker daraja-ai-door on daraja-studio.workers.dev running tools/ai-door/worker.js; ANTHROPIC_API_KEY stored as a SECRET, reading “Value encrypted”, unreadable by anyone including Jerry; the key “daraja-door” in the Claude Console with no expiry; the KV namespace daraja-door-count bound as DOOR_COUNT so the 40-asks-a-day-per-household cap counts; Cloudflare Access OFF; and the Worker allowing https://jerrywins1.github.io only. The cap was wired up BEFORE the endpoint was set, because worker.js skips counting entirely when DOOR_COUNT is missing and the account has auto-reload on — Jerry was asked and chose it that way, so the door never served an uncapped ask. TWO KEYS WERE BURNED AND BOTH REVOKED: one lost off the clipboard, one that went in as a plain variable rather than a secret and so was displayed in full and reached a screenshot. Neither was ever used by the Worker. If a key ever needs rotating, that is the same five minutes again. NO CLOUD CHAT CAN TEST THIS: the container gets a 403 from the egress proxy for workers.dev, so whether the door answers is always Jerry on a real device.
